about.title: Generation AI
privacy: Welcome to our Privacy Notice, designed to inform you about how we handle your personal data following the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) when you use our website featuring the GenAI Little Language Machine tool.

To make the subject matter of this notice clearer, let us define some terms from the GDPR. The "controller" refers to us, as we decide how and why your personal data is used, which also makes us responsible for protecting your personal data. "Personal data" includes any information that can identify you directly or indirectly, like your IP address. "Processing" covers all actions done with your data, such as collecting, storing, using, and deleting it.
It is important to read this notice to understand what data we collect from you, why we collect it, what we do with it, and what rights you have regarding your data.
If you have any questions about this notice, please reach out to the controller:
**Dr. Nicolas Pope**,
**Postal address:** University of Eastern Finland, Länsikatu 15, 80110 Joensuu, Finland.
**Email:** nicolas.pope@uef.fi
### 1. Data Processing Activity:
We log IP addresses.
However, we do not use cookies for tracking or analytics; instead, we provide content based solely on your inputs.
### 2. Purposes of Processing:
Logging IP addresses helps maintain website integrity and security by identifying and preventing malicious activities.
### 3. Legal Basis for Processing:

Primarily, we process IP addresses for security reasons, based on our legitimate interest in protecting our website and data as per Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. Again, we may also process data based on your consent under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR if you would like to exercise your right to access your logged IP address. In addition, we may process your personal data if we are instructed to do so by a competent court under Article 6(1)(c).
### 4. Legitimate Interests Pursued:
Our goal is to keep the website running by maintaining website integrity, and security, and preventing abuse.
### 5. Security:
We implement security measures to protect your IP addresses from unlawful access or damage. Your IP addresses are encrypted during any subsequent transfer.
### 6. Data Recipients:
Only authorized website personnel can access your IP address for security and maintenance purposes.
### 7. Data Transfers:
IP addresses may be transferred to Microsoft servers, but we ensure GDPR compliance for data protection.
### 8. Storage Limitation:
We keep IP addresses only as long as necessary, typically up to 7 days, unless required by law.
### 9. Your Rights:
Under GDPR, you have rights including

* Right to be informed: In addition to informing, you about processing purposes, retention periods, and to whom your data is shared, you have the right to be informed on how we collect. We collect your IP address when you visit our website.
* Right to access: you can request a copy of your logged IP address and associated log data.

* Right to rectification: if the logged data is inaccurate or incomplete, you can request rectification although IP address is not typically something that can be corrected in the same way as other data.
* Right to erasure: you can request deletion of your IP address within 7 days of your last visit to this website since your address is deleted automatically after 7 days.
* Right to object: you can object to the processing of your IP addresses.
* Right to lodge a complaint: you can lodge a complaint to the supervisory authority if you think that your data is not processed following GDPR provisions.
### 10. Updates to This Privacy Notice:
We may update this notice to reflect changes in our data processing practices or legal requirements. We will notify you of any changes.
We value your privacy and we are committed to protect your data and ensuring GDPR compliance. If you have questions or want to exercise your rights, contact us at nicolas.pope@uef.fi.

app.subtitle: Create your own tiny AI chatbot using these starting points.
app.saveMessage: Enter a name for your model:

confirmLoad.title: Continue Session
confirmLoad.message: A previous session was found. Do you want to load that model?

workflow.empty_desc: Design your model structure and start from scratch.
workflow.base_desc: Use a base model and adapt it to a new task with your data.
workflow.complete_desc: Cover all the stages in making a chatbot.
workflow.finetune_desc: Adjust the style and personality of an existing model.
workflow.advanced_desc: Access additional settings and features for advanced use.
workflow.model_desc: Select your model size and shape.
workflow.data_desc: Add your own text data for the model to learn from.

settings.title: Settings
settings.epochsHelp: Maximum number of times to loop through the entire training data. One epoch is one time through the data.
settings.mlpFactorHelp: Change the size of the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) in the transformer blocks. A larger MLP can allow the model to remember more patterns but will increase the number of parameters.
settings.headsHelp: Change the number of attention heads in the transformer blocks. More heads can allow the model to focus on different parts of the input simultaneously.
settings.contextHelp: The number of tokens the model can see to make its predictions.
settings.batchHelp: The number of samples processed at the same time to average out any problems.
settings.lrHelp: How fast to tune the parameters with each training step.
settings.temperatureHelp: Higher temperature produces more random outputs as it is less likely to select the most obvious next token.

data.title: Training Data
data.writeTip: Write or paste your own text data.
data.uploadTip: Upload files containing text data. Supported formats: txt, csv, pdf, docx.
data.dataHint: Use our dataset library to find text, or drop files here (txt, csv, pdf, docx) for training text. Any text can be used but there should be a lot.
data.textPlaceholder: Write or paste your own text here...

errors.fileLoadError: You can only drop files with text (txt, csv, pdf, docx).
errors.downloadLoadError: There was an unknown error loading the downloaded file.

data.help: A language model learns from example text. The more text you provide, the better it can learn. You can write your own text, upload files or use our dataset library.

checkmodel.title: Build Model
checkmodel.outdated: The model needs to be rebuilt
checkmodel.help: Building a model will allocate resources and assign random numbers to the parameters.
checkmodel.exceedsSizeLimit: The model has too many parameters.

confirm.title: Rebuild Model
confirm.message: Any training of the current model will be lost. Are you sure you want to rebuild the model?

model.title: Model
model.parametersHelp: The total number of numeric parameters in the model.
model.help: Your model stores the parameters and architecture that are adjusted during training and used to predict the next token.
model.visualHelp: This diagram shows the structure, or architecture, of your model. There are inputs, multiple layers of parameters and an output. You can edit the shape of the model to change the number of parameters and where they are placed.
model.archHelp: Select the size and shape of your language model before training it.

training.title: Training

errors.preparation: More training data is needed, at least a few thousand samples.
errors.noModel: Please load a model before training.
errors.notReady: Model or data is not ready for training.
errors.trainingFailed: Training this model failed. Refresh the page and try a smaller model or batch size.

training.help: The learning process where the parameters are slowly adjusted up or down until it can reproduce the patterns found in your example data. Time remaining is how long it will take to look at all of your data.
training.attentionHelp: A short example taken from your data. The model is trying to predict the highlighted token based on the previous text. The example is converted to numeric tokens. Each layer of the model pays attention to different parts of the text.
training.modelBoxHelp: Each layer of your model contributes towards the final prediction, one layer at a time. The parameters inside each layer are tuned by how well they contributed or not.
training.lossBoxHelp: After the model has made its prediction it is scored against the correct answer. Loss is a measure of how wrong the model's prediction was, so the training process tries to reduce this number.

errors.modelNotReady: Model is not ready for generation, try again in a moment.
errors.generationError: An unknown error occurred during text generation.

modelStatus.error: An error occurred with the model

validation.positive_integer: Value must be a positive integer
validation.nEmbed_divisible_nHead: Embedding size must be divisible by heads

tools.modelMissingHint: Please load a model and training data to view the training process.

training.title: Training Log
training.validationHelp: Some of your data is used to test how well the model is learning. This validation data is not shown to the model during training so it cannot cheat.
training.accuracyHelp: Accuracy is the percentage of predictions that were correct.
training.lossHelp: Loss is a measure of how wrong the model's predictions were. It refers to the loss of information.

tools.inferenceHint: Start generating text to see the animated visualisation of how it works.
tools.trainingHint: Start training to see the animated visualisation of how training works.
tools.sampleHelp: Your prompt, and any text already generated by a previous step, is tokenised and used as input to the model.
tools.dataHelp: Your tokenised training data provides a source of examples when training. It is not available to the model when generating text after training.

tokeniser.title: Vocabulary
tokeniser.invalidWarning: The vocabulary was not selected from the current data.
tokeniser.trainedWarning: The model is already trained, changing the vocabulary may cause problems.
tokeniser.help: The vocabulary is a set of letters, words or parts of words that are the building blocks of language for the model. These building blocks are called tokens and are assigned a unique number. Building a vocabulary will process your data to find the best tokens.

tokeniseData.title: Tokenise Data
tokeniseData.tooManyTokens: You have more tokens than needed
tokeniseData.help: Your text data needs to be split into the numeric tokens that the mathematical model can work with. Larger models need more tokens so the progress bar shows how many you may need.

finetune.title: Fine-tuning
finetune.warningContent: Fine-tuning is a work-in-progress feature. Please proceed with caution.

sharing.title: Sharing

sharing.option2_desc: Download a ZIP file containing your model that can be shared and loaded by others.
